title: MYOPATHY WITH RIGID SPINE, SCOLIOSIS, AND MALE-LIMITED HYPERGONADOTROPIC HYPOGONADISM

relationships.phenotype: MYOPATHY WITH RIGID SPINE, SCOLIOSIS, AND MALE-LIMITED HYPERGONADOTROPIC HYPOGONADISM

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that myopathy with rigid spine, scoliosis, and male-limited hypergonadotropic hypogonadism (MRSG) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the TBCE gene (604934) on chromosome 1q42.3.

checks.claim: Myopathy with rigid spine, scoliosis, and male-limited hypergonadotropic hypogonadism (MRSG) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the TBCE gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous pathogenic variant c.100 + 1G > A in TBCE was detected in three patients (P1-P3), followed by the confirmation of heterozygous carrier status of the variant in their parents.
checks.explanation: Paper supports homozygous TBCE mutation for this phenotype; it does not use the name MRSG or report compound heterozygous cases for this phenotype.

checks.claim: The TBCE gene is located on chromosome 1q42.3.
checks.evidence_quote: Inactivating mutations within the TBCE, which encodes a tubulin folding cofactor E essential for tubulin folding and polymerization
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature, not stated in the paper but acceptable.

paragraphs.text: MRSG is a TBCE-related disorder that is milder than other phenotypes associated with TBCE variants. Features include amyotrophy, testicular failure, and mild intellectual disability, with or without short stature (Sparber et al., 2025). Badura-Stronka et al. (2025) described later onset than in other TBCE-related disease, rigid spine, proximal muscle atrophy, scoliosis, cryptorchidism in males, neutropenia, eosinophilia, and nocturnal hypoxemia.

checks.claim: MRSG is a TBCE-related disorder that is milder than other phenotypes associated with TBCE variants.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous carriers of the c.100 + 1G > A variant exhibit a markedly milder clinical course, with no deviations in the calcium-phosphate metabolism and central nervous system pathology in MRI studies.

checks.claim: Features of MRSG include amyotrophy, testicular failure, and mild intellectual disability, with or without short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: presenting with amyotrophy, testicular failure, and mild intellectual disability, with or without short stature.

checks.claim: MRSG has a later onset than other TBCE-related disease.
checks.evidence_quote: The primary clinical differences compared to homozygous c.464 T > A individuals include the onset of symptoms at a later developmental stage, normal motor development, eventual proper speech development, and cryptorchidism in boys.

checks.claim: Features of MRSG include rigid spine, proximal muscle atrophy, scoliosis, cryptorchidism in males, neutropenia, eosinophilia, and nocturnal hypoxemia.
checks.evidence_quote: Muscle atrophy primarily affects proximal muscles, and increased muscle tone is most pronounced in the paraspinal muscles, leading to spinal mobility limitations. Furthermore, patients exhibited recurrent infections, neutropenia, eosinophilia, and nocturnal hypoxemia.
checks.explanation: Scoliosis and cryptorchidism are also noted elsewhere (discussion/conclusion).

paragraphs.text: Badura-Stronka et al. (2025) reported a 13-year-old Polish girl (P1) with no significant family history. She was born at term with normal birth weight, walked independently at 14 months, and had slight speech delay. At age 6 years she developed muscle weakness and limited mobility of the cervical spine, with increased paraspinal muscle tone. The rigid spine progressed to involve the thoracic and lumbar segments, and thoracic scoliosis worsened from age 11. At 13 years she had proximal muscle weakness, limb muscle atrophy, diminished tendon reflexes, waddling gait, and weight and height below the 3rd percentile. She had nocturnal hypoxemia with central and obstructive apneas that required nocturnal noninvasive ventilation. She also had osteoporosis (T-score -3.9), eosinophilia, neutropenia, and platelet anisocytosis.

paragraphs.text: Badura-Stronka et al. (2025) also reported a 20-year-old Polish man (P2) with bilateral cryptorchidism and mildly delayed motor and speech development. He had febrile seizures from age 4 years during episodes of recurrent pneumonia and generalized muscle pain from age 5. At age 11 he had contractures and distal limb paresis, and muscle biopsy showed mild, nonspecific myopathic changes. From age 13 he had limited spine mobility, shoulder girdle atrophy, and nocturnal hypoxemia that required noninvasive ventilation. MRI showed atrophy and fatty infiltration of the paraspinal, iliopsoas, gluteal, and thigh muscles. Other features included gynecomastia at age 14, thoracic scoliosis, strabismus, high palate, inability to flex the thoracic and lumbar spine, and persistent eosinophilia and neutropenia from age 10. EMG showed moderate myogenic features.

paragraphs.text: The third patient reported by Badura-Stronka et al. (2025) was an 18-year-old Ukrainian man (P3) with bilateral inguinal cryptorchidism, which was treated by orchidopexy at ages 3 and 4 years. From age 3 he had recurrent respiratory infections, otitis, and bronchitis. He underwent gonadectomy at ages 10 and 15 years. Histology showed atrophic and sclerotic testes with no spermatogenesis. He had intellectual disability, dysmorphic features, and neutropenia, but his motor development was normal.

paragraphs.text: Badura-Stronka et al. (2025) systematically reviewed 98 previously reported patients with TBCE variants together with their own 3 patients. They concluded that homozygosity for c.100+1G-A causes a milder course than other TBCE variants. Patients with this genotype had later onset (mean age 5 years), normal motor development, eventually normal speech, normal calcium-phosphate metabolism, and no significant changes on CNS MRI. Their distinctive features included cryptorchidism in males, rigid spine, proximal muscle atrophy, scoliosis, neutropenia, eosinophilia, and nocturnal hypoxemia. By contrast, patients homozygous for c.155_166del had the HRDS/KCS1 phenotype, and patients with c.464T-A had severe neurodevelopmental disease without genital abnormalities.
